evals.name: no-linting-ts-repo
evals.prompt: We're a 5-person team on a TypeScript/React codebase. We have zero linting or type checking configured — just tsc errors we mostly ignore. What should we set up?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to adopt a TypeScript-aware linter (ESLint/typescript-eslint or Biome) starting from a recommended preset, strict tsc, and guidance on running checks at more than one stage (editor, pre-commit, CI).
assertions: Output must recommend a TypeScript-aware linter (ESLint/typescript-eslint or Biome)
Output must mention running checks at more than one stage (e.g. editor, pre-commit, CI)
Output must not recommend writing tests as the primary fix for a missing linting/type-checking setup

evals.name: python-no-type-safety
evals.prompt: Our Python codebase has no type hints and no static type checking — bugs keep slipping through that a type checker would catch. What do you recommend?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation for a Python type checker (mypy, Pyright, or Pyre) plus Ruff for lint/format, with incremental adoption guidance rather than flipping strict mode everywhere at once.
assertions: Output must recommend a Python type checker (mypy, Pyright, or Pyre)
Output must recommend a linter/formatter distinct from the type checker (e.g. Ruff)
Output must not conflate linting and type checking as if they were the same tool

evals.name: pre-commit-vs-ci-only
evals.prompt: Should we run our linter as a pre-commit hook, or just in CI?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation for both, tiered — fast checks pre-commit, full suite in CI — justified by how fast modern Rust-based linters have become.
assertions: Output must recommend running checks at both pre-commit and CI stages, not just one
Output must justify pre-commit feasibility using check speed
Output must not recommend disabling or skipping pre-commit hooks in favor of CI-only checks

evals.name: existing-linter-permissive-preset
evals.prompt: We already have ESLint configured on our repo, but it only catches the bare minimum — most real bugs still slip through review. Should we replace it with something else?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to keep ESLint and tighten its rule set/preset (e.g. move toward typescript-eslint strict, add missing plugins) rather than replacing the tool outright.
assertions: Output must recommend strengthening the existing ESLint configuration rather than replacing the tool
Output must reference a specific rule set or preset to move toward, not just 'more rules'
Output must not recommend switching to a different linter as the primary fix

evals.name: semantic-bug-no-lint-rule
evals.prompt: We had a production bug where a discount was applied twice because the logic didn't match our pricing spec. No lint rule would have caught this. How do we prevent this kind of thing?
evals.expected_output: An explanation that this is outside what static analysis can catch, with a recommendation to use an AI-assisted code review skill/agent as a complement to linting for semantic/business-logic judgment calls, not a proposal to invent a lint rule for it.
assertions: Output must explain that this kind of bug is outside what a linter or type checker can catch
Output must recommend an AI-assisted review skill or agent as a complement for this kind of semantic check
Output must not propose a specific lint rule as the fix for a business-logic/semantic bug
